Common Days Cafe / INS Studio
articles.summary: Located in Maros, a small town on the outskirts of Makassar, Indonesia, this project occupies a newly developed commercial district where the urban fabric remains relatively sparse, allowing the surrounding natural landscape to remain a defining presence. Conceived as a gathering space, the building is organized across three levels, each accommodating a distinct program while collectively encouraging social interaction, work, and community activities.

articles.title: Junohair Sung-Su 2nd Salon / TYPE S
articles.summary: Sung-su is one of the most distinctive neighborhoods in South Korea. Built upon a long-established industrial landscape, the area has continuously evolved into a destination where new cultures and experiences emerge. Today, it attracts visitors who seek novelty and a sense of rarity. Against this unique local context, Juno Hair Sung-su aimed to create contrasting spatial images within the salon.

articles.title: Sartoriale Offices / DOS - G arquitectos
articles.summary: Located in Panama City, the new Sartoriale offices were conceived as a spatial interpretation of the values that define the real estate developer: tradition, craftsmanship, and bespoke design. The project proposes a working environment where the daily experience reflects the company's culture and its understanding of living spaces.

articles.title: Castelo House / Gonçalo Grácio
articles.summary: The house is located in a historic context, within the medieval town of Castelo de Vide . The project sought to enhance the authenticity of the site and respect the pre-existing structure, preserving its intimate spatial logic.

articles.title: Villa Arena / Ábaton
articles.summary: Villa Arena is a project conceived with a deep sensitivity towards family life. The commission came from a family of six seeking a place devoted to calm, togetherness, and contemplation within the coastal landscape of Cádiz.

articles.title: How the Arts and Crafts Movement Still Shapes Contemporary Architecture
articles.summary: The Arts and Crafts movement is often remembered as an architectural style defined by handcrafted details, an intimate scale, natural materials, and a rejection of excess and industry. Its influence is frequently traced through visual characteristics that continue to appear in contemporary architecture and interiors , from exposed timber and crafted joinery to an emphasis on texture and permanence, yet reducing the movement to an aesthetic vocabulary overlooks its far more significant contribution.
